rationale: Today's long-form is a Lane A search-question video, not news. Lane C CagriSema-in-women is a 20 Oct post hoc result with only press coverage, too thin for 8–15 min and the fact-check, so it becomes a Short. 'Tirzepatide Side Effects' overlaps the 10-17 SURMOUNT-5 GI Short. Plateau overlaps yesterday's 'How Long Does Tirzepatide Take to Work?' long-form and its Short. Stopping has been covered 3 times in 30 days. So L1 is 'What to Eat on Tirzepatide (Mounjaro)', a playbook Lane A title. It is evergreen, has a New Year search spike, and is fully verifiable from the 2025 joint nutrition advisory, US dietary guidance and the labels. The Conversation's Oct 20 guide is the intro hook. Shorts follow the slot plan. 13:00 lead: a gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Short correcting the Mounjaro/Zepbound recall-headline confusion, a new fact distinct from yesterday's Houston RX Short. 08:00: Lane C news in Short form (CagriSema in women by menopause stage, within 48 h). 20:00 funnel: a spin-off of L1, run after L1 is live at 14:00 so the 'Full breakdown' CTA names a published video. The carousel is minimum-effort, reusing the verified 10-19 surgery Short text. Pillars rotate with no repeats: life-on-glp1, myths, research, get-the-most, beyond-weight. Mix: 1 emerging, 1 peaking myth-correction, 2 evergreen, 1 reuse. No 'approved yet?', no 'Did X beat Y?', no list titles in Shorts, and every Short names a drug.

pieces.topic: What to eat on tirzepatide (and semaglutide): protein, fibre, fluids and easier meals when appetite drops, based on the 2025 joint nutrition advisory (ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS) and dietary guidelines
pieces.angle: Lane A, 'Life on GLP-1'. Hook (15 s or less) with no news peg: 'When tirzepatide turns your appetite down, what you eat matters more. By the end you'll know what experts recommend for protein, fiber, fluids and easier meals.' First answer: the 2025 joint advisory from four US nutrition and obesity groups recommends building smaller meals around a protein food, adding fiber gradually and drinking fluids through the day. Chapters as planned. Every habit is 'recommended by the advisory/guidelines', never 'proven on tirzepatide'. Include the kidney-disease protein caveat, the fluid-restriction caveat, 'start strength training gently', the GI side effects, 'don't change your medicines on your own', and the full prescriber line, plus 'consider asking for a registered dietitian referral'.
pieces.working_title: What to Eat on Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Protein, Fibre, Meals
pieces.why: Playbook Lane A title with top practical search demand from new starters and a timely Oct 20 hook. It rests on settled guideline evidence, so it can pass the fact-check, and it doesn't repeat any Short from the last 14 days. | fact-check: Good Lane A topic: people search for it, it's evergreen and safe if habits stay 'recommended'. One problem: I couldn't find a Conversation nutrition guide for new GLP-1 starters dated Oct 20, 2026. The closest Conversation piece is an older one about raising your own GLP-1 through food ('What and how you eat can increase the effects of GLP-1 without drugs'). That's a different topic and isn't about medicine users. Don't hang the hook on a source we can't confirm. Build the script on the 2025 joint nutrition advisory (ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS) plus national dietary guidelines and the drug labels (for delayed stomach emptying and GI side effects). Give protein amounts only as the advisory's 'recommended' ranges, and say 'check with your clinician first if you have kidney disease or have been told to limit protein'. Fluids: 'unless you've been told to limit fluids'. Fibre: 'build up gradually'. No calorie targets, no meal-skipping, no 'GLP-1 diet' claims. Mention nausea, constipation and diarrhoea as common, usually mild to moderate. Only name 'How Long Does Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Take to Work?' as watch-next if it is already published with that exact title; otherwise name another published Lane A video or say 'follow for more'. Small title fix: most of our audience is US and searches 'fiber', so use 'What to Eat on Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Protein, Fiber, Meals' (60 characters or fewer). Log lane A.

pieces.topic: 'Mounjaro and Zepbound recall' headlines vs what the FDA enforcement report actually lists: a Class II recall (classified Oct 8, 2026) of 22 multi-dose vials of compounded tirzepatide for lack of assurance of sterility
pieces.angle: Title: 'Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: What the FDA Actually Listed #shorts'. Answer by 10 s: 'Per the FDA Enforcement Report, a Class II recall classified [exact FDA date], 2026 covers 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide from Apothecary Pharma, not branded pens [only if confirmed on publish day].' One line: compounded drugs aren't FDA-approved, and anything injected has to be sterile. One line on what Class II means, in FDA wording. Action: check the FDA recall listings and ask your pharmacist or prescriber. Don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Prescriber line. 170 words or fewer. No sellers, no sourcing, no emoji, no #Mounjaro or #Zepbound.
pieces.working_title: Mounjaro or Zepbound Recalled? What the FDA Actually Listed #shorts
pieces.why: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' is our strongest Short lane (median 108). Oct 20 headlines tied brand names to a compounded recall, which causes search confusion we can calmly correct with a new FDA fact. | fact-check: The core record checks out in coverage of the FDA enforcement report: Apothecary Pharma LLC (Cary, NC) voluntarily recalled 22 vials of compounded tirzepatide (18 mg/mL, 4 mL multidose vials) for lack of assurance of sterility, and it was classified Class II. Three problems: (1) Date. Secondary sources give the classification as Oct 10, 2026, not Oct 8 (the recall began Sept 24). Take the date from the FDA Enforcement Report entry itself and use exactly that. (2) It isn't the only one. Houston RX recalled 64 vials of compounded tirzepatide-niacinamide (Class II, sterility, started Sept 25), and Carolina Infusion is also mentioned. Our 10-20 S1 seems to have used '64 vials', so this may repeat yesterday's topic. To pass the variety guard, the piece must add a new fact: the 22-vial Apothecary listing and the 'branded-name headline vs compounded record' point. It must not re-tell Houston RX. Don't say 'the recall' as if there were only one. Say 'recent FDA-listed recalls of compounded tirzepatide'. (3) Title: putting Mounjaro and Zepbound first, on a compounded recall, makes it look like the branded drugs were recalled, and our craft rules ban brand tags on compounded-recall posts. Only say 'no branded Mounjaro or Zepbound pens were listed' if a search of the FDA Enforcement Report on publish day confirms it, credited and dated. Give the Class II definition in FDA wording. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved or reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality. No emoji, no brand hashtags.

pieces.topic: CagriSema in women: Novo Nordisk's REDEFINE 1 post hoc analyses at the Menopause Society meeting (Oct 20, 2026), with weight loss by menopause stage
pieces.angle: Title: 'CagriSema in Women: Did Menopause Stage Change the Result? #shorts'. By 10 s: 'In a post hoc look at Novo Nordisk's REDEFINE 1 trial, presented Oct 20, 2026, women on CagriSema lost 25.0% on average at 68 weeks versus 3.0% on placebo. By menopause stage: 26.7%, 24.8% and 23.1% versus 2.1%, 1.7% and 2.6% on placebo. That's numerically similar, but it wasn't formally tested, and stage was estimated after the fact.' Population: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. Investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. GI side effects line. Prescriber line about approved options or trials.
pieces.working_title: CagriSema in Women: Did Menopause Stage Change the Result? #shorts
pieces.why: New named result within the 48 h window with low competition, aimed at the large 40–60 women's audience. Breaking-news findings belong in a Short, not a long-form. | fact-check: Fresh news (Oct 20, 2026; Novo Nordisk release via PR Newswire), so it qualifies as a first explainer. The figures check out against Novo's release: 2,309 women, CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg, 25.0% vs 3.0% placebo at week 68. In the menopause analysis (1,902 women): premenopausal 26.7%, perimenopausal 24.8%, postmenopausal 23.1%, with placebo at 2.1%, 1.7% and 2.6%. Fixes: (1) Don't say 'results were similar'. Novo says p-values weren't adjusted for multiplicity and differences by subgroup weren't formally tested. Menopause stage was assigned after the fact from age, history and symptoms, not measured. Say 'numerically similar; not formally compared'. (2) Group sizes: use the women-only analysis numbers (2,309 overall, 1,902 by stage, plus arm splits if Novo or the abstract give them). Don't use REDEFINE 1's full trial size. If arm splits aren't published, say only the total and 'women in the trial'. (3) Confirm the estimand label from Novo's release or the abstract. Don't assume 'efficacy estimand'. (4) Every placebo figure goes next to its CagriSema figure, especially on screen. (5) Status: investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. Before stating any filing status, cite a recent dated Novo or FDA source; a filing isn't approval. The title's question must be answered within 10 s: 'average loss was numerically similar across stages, but the analysis wasn't designed to test differences.' Mention common GI side effects. Point to a prescriber about approved options or trials. No online sourcing. 'Follow for more'.

pieces.topic: Eating less on tirzepatide: why protein at each meal matters for keeping muscle, per the 2025 joint nutrition advisory and the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy
pieces.angle: Run at 20:00 the day after L1 is live. Title: 'Eating Less on Tirzepatide: Are You Getting Enough Protein? #shorts'. By 10 s: 'When appetite drops, protein can drop too. In a SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, about a quarter of the weight lost on tirzepatide over 72 weeks was lean mass, which includes muscle [exact figure and per-arm substudy sizes from the paper].' Recommended by the 2025 joint nutrition advisory: a protein food at each meal from varied sources, unless your clinician has told you to limit protein (for example, kidney disease), plus strength training, starting gently. One GI line. Prescriber line. Last line: 'Full breakdown: [exact published L1 title], on our channel.' The link goes in the pinned comment and the first description line.
pieces.working_title: Eating Less on Tirzepatide? Are You Getting Enough Protein? #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1 that sends viewers to today's long-form. It uses the muscle-outcome question format (100 and 131 views) instead of a how-to list. | fact-check: A good funnel concept, but four fixes: (1) Timing. The playbook says funnel Shorts run the day after their long-form, and only once it's live. Schedule S3 for the 20:00 slot on the day after L1 publishes, and use L1's final published title word for word (it may become 'Fiber'). (2) Framing. The SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy measured lean mass, which isn't the same as muscle. It also includes water, organs and connective tissue. Say 'about a quarter of the weight lost was lean mass, which includes muscle'. Never say 'a quarter was muscle'. Take the exact proportion, the substudy group sizes (substudy participants by arm, not SURMOUNT-1's full enrolment) and the 72-week timepoint from the published paper. Give the placebo comparison for context. (3) Variety guard. Earlier Shorts ('Fat or muscle?', 'How to protect your muscle') probably used this same substudy. Lead with the new fact, the 2025 joint advisory's recommendation to prioritise protein when intake drops, and keep SURMOUNT-1 to one supporting line. (4) Keep 'recommended by the advisory', never 'proven on tirzepatide'. Include the kidney/protein-limit caveat, 'start strength training gently', one GI line and the prescriber line. Title: two stacked questions are weaker; answer the question within 10 s.

pieces.topic: GLP-1 medicines and surgery outcomes: 2.03 million elective-surgery records linked GLP-1 use to lower odds of major heart complications and infections (ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026, observational), reused from the verified 10-19 Short
pieces.angle: Minimum-effort carousel built only from the verified 10-19 Short script, with no new research. Slides: 1. the question; 2. the finding, '11% lower odds of major heart complications, 8% lower odds of infection, linked to, not proof', in the Short's exact wording; 3. population: adults, elective surgery over 1 hour, at least 24 h in hospital, 2016–2024, 145,610 on a GLP-1, conference data; 4. why: these medicines can slow stomach emptying, so tell your surgeon and anesthesia team and follow their plan; 5. common GI side effects and 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own'; 6. disclaimer plus full prescriber line.
